reason: The text, from Nehemiah 5, explicitly portrays the elite unfavorably. Nehemiah confronts the nobles and officials (חֹרִים וְסְגָנִים) for exacting usury from their fellow Jews and enslaving their own brothers' children. The text further describes the former governors (פַּחוֹת הָרִאשֹׁנִים) as burdensome, taking bread and wine from the people for payment and allowing their servants to oppress the populace. This portrayal establishes the elite as exploitative and oppressive. Nehemiah's own conduct is presented as a righteous contrast—he explicitly states he did not demand the governor's allowance because of fear of God and the heavy burden on the people, thereby emphasizing the moral culpability of the preceding elite.
